# Unified requires first study

The `first-observations.json` bundle retains every original UTF-8 byte, path,
mode and SHA-256 from two pre-implementation temporary studies: 51 mixed
constraint files and 38 order-study files. These are fourteen complete first
sources and their manifests, expectations, actual stdout/stderr, observations
and original assessments. No original source or diagnostic was repaired in place.
The bundle is a new static history input; it executes no recorded command.

The informed author had the specifications, Issues and repository available.
The fixed CLI and checker identities stayed unchanged, with at most one quantum
wire. Six cases succeeded and eight rejected. Native process counts were not
instrumented; the recorded expected stages are not observed invocation counts.

The first false closed premise reports the entire declaration. The later
guard-order question was explicitly unknown before observation: a preceding
`n >= 1` admits `n-1`, while the reverse order rejects the subtraction. This
records actual behavior separately from the subsequent Reference clarification.
Simple comparison reordering succeeds. Nonlinear symbolic multiplication and
missing direct access reject even for convenient closed values or empty folds.

The fixed integrity reader is `scripts/test_unified_requires_baseline.py`,
called by the ordinary Rust baseline test. Later implementation, CLI replay,
mixed-constraint and stale-evidence tests are separate evidence. Neither the
study nor source identity proves source/runtime preservation, arbitrary-family
correctness or constitutional discharge. Work is tracked in Issue #47.
